clinicalPearls: An autosomal dominant disorder of keratinisation caused by variants in LOR, which encodes loricrin, a major protein of the cornified cell envelope
Presents as a mutilating (Vohwinkel-like) palmoplantar keratoderma combined with a generalised ichthyosis
The palmoplantar keratoderma typically has a honeycomb surface and may show starfish-shaped keratoses over the knuckles
Constricting fibrous bands (pseudo-ainhum) can form around digits and threaten autoamputation
Unlike classic connexin-related Vohwinkel syndrome, the loricrin variant is associated with ichthyosis rather than sensorineural deafness
Diagnosis is clinical, supported by biopsy showing hyperkeratosis with retained nuclei and by LOR molecular testing
Management is supportive with keratolytics, emollients and foot care, oral retinoids for severe keratoderma, and surgical release of constricting bands where necessary
reference.pathophysiology: Loricrin keratoderma arises from frameshift variants in LOR that alter loricrin, the principal structural protein of the cornified cell envelope. The mutant protein carries an abnormal carboxy-terminal extension with a nuclear localisation signal, causing it to be mistargeted to the nucleus rather than incorporated correctly into the cornified envelope. Defective envelope assembly impairs the epidermal barrier and terminal differentiation, producing generalised ichthyosis and a thick mutilating palmoplantar keratoderma, with chronic fibrosis around digits generating pseudo-ainhum.
additionalDifferentials: Vohwinkel syndrome due to GJB2 (connexin 26) with deafness
additionalInvestigations: Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis with retained nuclei (parakeratosis) in the stratum corneum
Examination for pseudo-ainhum and starfish keratoses
Audiological assessment to distinguish from connexin-related Vohwinkel syndrome
Assessment of foot and hand function
redFlags: Deep secondary infection of fissured keratoderma
Rapid or asymmetrical change raising concern for malignant transformation
Severe functional impairment of hands or feet
reference.prognosis: The disorder is lifelong; with keratolytic and emollient care, retinoids and timely surgical release of constricting bands most patients preserve function, though pseudo-ainhum and disability can complicate severe disease.
pitfalls: Confusing it with connexin-related Vohwinkel syndrome and overlooking the associated ichthyosis
Missing early pseudo-ainhum before irreversible digital constriction
Failing to arrange audiology to distinguish the two forms of mutilating keratoderma
Delaying surgical release of constricting bands
management: Provide intensive topical care with emollients and keratolytics such as urea or salicylic acid to soften the palmoplantar keratoderma and ichthyosis
Use systemic retinoids such as acitretin to reduce hyperkeratosis in severe disease, monitoring for their side effects
Arrange timely surgical or medical release of constricting fibrous bands (pseudo-ainhum) to prevent digital strangulation and autoamputation
Treat secondary bacterial or fungal infection of fissured hyperkeratotic skin
Support hand and foot function with podiatry, physiotherapy and appropriate footwear
Distinguish from connexin-related Vohwinkel syndrome with audiological assessment given the differing associations
Offer genetic counselling for this autosomal dominant LOR disorder with family screening
Coordinate lifelong care through dermatology, clinical genetics and surgical teams, escalating urgently for threatened digits
